expectations.text: Opens with a hook rather than throat-clearing scene-setting
expectations.evidence: "Truth be told, I auditioned for a lead role in this year's Christmas drama. Cast list went up, and I was a side character." -- 'Truth be told' matches Asher's confirmed 2016 usage exactly.

expectations.text: Admits the initial disappointment plainly, without over-apologizing
expectations.evidence: "A bit disappointing, not gonna lie." -- stated once, plainly, no repeated hedging.

expectations.text: Contains at least one H2 header phrased as a question
expectations.evidence: "So What Do You Do With a Side Character?" and "What Happens When You Forget Your One Line?"

expectations.text: Includes the improvised-line anecdote with concrete specific detail
expectations.evidence: "Dress rehearsal. My one line was gone. Completely gone. I froze for a second... then just said something... It worked. Genuinely worked better than the line that was written."

expectations.text: Ending is a genuine reflective callback rather than a generic moral-of-the-story wrap-up
expectations.evidence: "The role I didn't want ended up giving me the one moment from this whole production I'll actually remember." -- directly reuses the lead/side-character tension set up in paragraph 1.

expectations.text: Does not contain banned buzzwords or invented fake-profound kicker phrasing
expectations.evidence: None present; ending stays grounded in the concrete anecdote.

expectations.text: Uses short paragraphs and at least one deliberate fragment or ellipsis
expectations.evidence: "Dress rehearsal. My one line was gone. Completely gone." and consistently short paragraphs throughout.

claims.claim: Checked the emotional beat against a real 2016 example before writing it, rather than inventing a voice
claims.evidence: Transcript cites the 2016 Christmas post excerpt in voice-examples.md ('Truth be told, I was a little disappointed that I didn't get to play the role of the Candyman') as calibration before drafting the near-identical beat here.

claims.claim: Caught and fixed an internal consistency error (invented 'two scenes' contradicting the vaguer 'a handful of scenes')
claims.evidence: Transcript documents this fix during the no-ai-slop pass; final post reads 'A handful of scenes' consistently.

eval_feedback.overall: Strongest of the three with-skill runs -- the executor's use of voice-examples.md as calibration evidence (not just rules) is exactly the intended workflow.
